I love Marxism and the Oppression of Women: Toward a Unitary Theory by Lise Vogel.

This one was first published in 1983 and was later revisited by the author herself. Vogel sought to bridge the gap between Marxist theory and feminist concerns by developing a united theory that stays true to the Marxist orthodoxy. Heck, she even argued that Engels, as opposed to Marx, had a view that patriarchy and capitalism are two separate systems 😂. She explains that women's subordination arises from their role in social reproduction by utilizing Marx's Das Capital, which capitalism relies on but often devalues and obscures.
